stemMd: Exactly two of three switches P, Q and R are on. If P is on, Q is off. If R is off, P is on. Which switch must be on?
explanationMd: If R were off, P would be on, which would force Q off. That would leave only one switch on, contradicting the total of two. Therefore R is on. Either P or Q can supply the second on switch.

distractorRationale.e: Q and R can be on while P is off.
distractorRationale.c: P and R can be on while Q is off.
distractorRationale.d: Exactly two switches are on, so one of them must be on.
distractorRationale.a: The first condition permits exactly two, not three.
